function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** that you can copy‑paste into your terminal (or run in a script).  
I’ve also included the exact file contents that should be added to the repository.

> **NOTE** – I can’t actually clone or push to the repo from here, but the commands below will do it for you on your machine.

---

## 1️⃣ Clone the repository

```bash
git clone git@github.com:zelarhq/nodejs-welcome.git
cd nodejs-welcome
```

---

## 2️⃣ Analyse the repo & create the required files

> The repo is a tiny Node.js “Hello World” app (likely an Express server listening on port 3000).  
> We’ll create:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Build a lightweight Docker image |
| `k8s/deployment.yaml` + `k8s/service.yaml` | Deploy to Kubernetes |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI pipeline that builds & pushes the image |

### 2.1 Dockerfile

Create a file named `Dockerfile` at the **root** of the repo:

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Use the official Node.js 18 Alpine image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first (so we can cache npm install)
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> **Why node:18-alpine?**  
> It’s small, secure, and the latest LTS that the repo probably targets.

---

### 2.2 Kubernetes manifests

Create a directory `k8s/` and inside it two files:

#### `k8s/deployment.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:latest   # will be overridden by the CI build tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
```

#### `k8s/service.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - port: 80          # external port
    targetPort: 3000  # container port
```

> **Tip:** If you want a LoadBalancer or NodePort, change `type` accordingly.

---

### 2.3 GitHub Actions workflow

Create the directory `.github/workflows/` and add a file `ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # Checkout the repo
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      # Set up Node.js
      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'

      # Install dependencies
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # Run tests (optional – remove if no tests)
      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test || true

      # Build Docker image
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: |
          docker build -t zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .
          echo "${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}" | docker login -u "${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}" --password-stdin
          docker push zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}

      # (Optional) Deploy to Kubernetes – uncomment if you want auto‑deploy
      # - name: Deploy to Kubernetes
      #   uses: azure/k8s-deploy@v3
      #   with:
      #     manifests: |
      #       ./k8s/deployment.yaml
      #       ./k8s/service.yaml
      #     images: zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
      #     kubeconfig: ${{ secrets.KUBECONFIG }}
```

> **What you need to set up in GitHub Secrets:**
> * `DOCKER_USERNAME` – your Docker Hub username
> * `DOCKER_PASSWORD` – your Docker Hub password (or a personal access token)
> * `KUBECONFIG` – optional, if you enable the auto‑deploy step

---

## 3️⃣ Add the new files to Git

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml k8s/service.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
```

---

## 4️⃣ Commit & push

```bash
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and GitHub Actions CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

---

### Quick sanity check

After pushing, you should see:

* A **Docker image** tagged with the commit SHA in Docker Hub (`zelarhq/nodejs-welcome:<sha>`).
* A **GitHub Actions** run that builds the image and pushes it.
* (If you enabled the deploy step) A **Kubernetes deployment** and service created in your cluster.

---

## Recap of the files created

```
nodejs-welcome/
├── Dockerfile
├── k8s/
│   ├── deployment.yaml
│   └── service.yaml
└── .github/
    └── workflows/
        └── ci.yml
```

Feel free to tweak the Docker image tag, replica count, or service type to match your production needs. Happy coding!
